newsitem.title: GERMANY: Top Kohl aide warns against German reshuffle talk.
newsitem.headline: Top Kohl aide warns against German reshuffle talk.

text.p: The parliamentary leader of German Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU) has urged the ruling coalition not to be distracted from key issues by talk of a cabinet reshuffle.

Wolfgang Schaeuble told the daily Sueddeutsche Zeitung in an interview to be published on Wednesday that the alliance should focus on pushing through reforms blocked by the opposition Social Democrats (SPD) in the upper house of parliament.

"Now we must do all we can to at least partly break through the SPD blockade in the Bundesrat," Schaeuble was quoted as saying in response to a question about Finance Minister Theo Waigel's recent call for a cabinet reshuffle this year.
"We should not be distracted from solving the main problems by getting involved in a debate about personnel," he said.
In interviews on Sunday, Waigel called on Kohl to replace several ministers in his 17-member cabinet before launching the 1998 election campaign.

Kohl, who is currently on holiday in Austria, sought on Monday to quash speculation a cabinet shuffle was imminent. A government spokesman said the chancellor had no plans to replace any of his ministers.
The denial failed to quell the sudden revival of speculation that Kohl will shake up his cabinet before the elections due in September 1998.

Schaeuble, who is Kohl's chief lieutenant in the CDU, said he had himself not spoken to Waigel and did not know exactly what the minister had in mind. He said he agreed with Kohl that reshuffle talk was superfluous.
Using its majority in the Bundesrat, the SPD early last month blocked a major government tax reform aimed at relieving the tax burden by 30 billion marks.
